initial:
Use case: compositing / modular game environment illustration.
Input image: edit target and exact visual style reference, a Chinese dark underworld game level map. Preserve its hand-painted charcoal black rock, misty ink-gray jagged mountains, muted crimson river, dim red lanterns, twisted dead trees, ruined Chinese architecture, and fine painterly details.

Primary request: REDESIGN the artwork as a production modular horizontal map tileset. Create one 3:1 landscape atlas (3072x1024 preferred) containing EXACTLY FOUR equal 3:4 portrait tiles side by side with ZERO spacing, zero borders, zero labels. They will be cut at 25%, 50%, 75% width. From left to right: tile 1 entry gate, tile 2 stone arch bridge over crimson river, tile 3 ruined paifang and rope bridge, tile 4 final underworld palace with stairs. This is NOT merely a panorama split into four. The legal strings are 1(2|3)*4, including 14,1234,124,134,1224,13234,1334. Each interior tile must tile with itself or the other in either order.

MOST IMPORTANT: all connectable vertical edges must use exactly THE SAME full-height interface design with matching texture, color, horizon and path geometry. This includes the RIGHT edge of tile 1, BOTH edges of tile 2, BOTH edges of tile 3, and the LEFT edge of tile 4. Reserve 12% of each tile width at these edges for an identical quiet neutral connecting landscape. At every such edge: upper 0-37% cloudy charcoal gray sky and distant low silhouetted mountains; 37-51% soft gray mist and subdued far cliffs; 51-57% flat dark gray rocky ground; 57-63% a level dusty muted red path passing exactly horizontally across the edge at y=60% of image height, with matching 6% width; 63-79% uninterrupted dark craggy cliff face; 79-100% pale gray mist and distant dark low rocks. Keep the sky neutral gray at ALL connecting edges. All connectable edges must have identical brightness, color, shapes and path y. Nearby road must be straight and level for at least 10% tile width before bending inward. Do not cut large objects at these edges. No branches, chains, bridges, lanterns, moons, buildings, waterfalls crossing a connecting edge. Unique objects must remain within each tile's central 70%. The bridge in tile 2 and rope bridge in tile 3 connect to the same level red road at both tile edges. Each tile should be visually varied in its middle, with winding road and explorable platforms but controlled identical outer interfaces. Entry gate in tile 1 and final palace in tile 4 are at the NON-connecting ends. The red moon should be fully contained in tile 4 and not cut by any tile boundary.

Keep the reference's beautiful intricate painterly fantasy art. No human figures, no user interface, no numbered level markers, no text, no watermark. Fill the canvas completely. Exact matching edge architecture is more important than dramatic changing perspective.
refinement:
Edit this modular game-map atlas with exactly FOUR equal 543x724 tiles arranged horizontally in a 2172x724 image. Preserve the beautiful dark Chinese underworld hand-painted style, all four central scenic identities, same scale, image dimensions and tile positions.

Fix only the production defects:
1. REMOVE every black vertical divider/border at x=543, x=1086 and x=1629. There must be NO lines, NO gutters, NO drawn tile frames, NO straight rectangular edging. Continuous natural landscape all the way across.
2. Make every tile connection share the same subdued gray clouds, far misty mountains, foreground cliff and pale fog at corresponding vertical coordinates. Use ONE shared quiet interface. At each x=543,1086,1629 crossing and both left and right edges of the middle two tiles, a single dusty muted-crimson road must cross HORIZONTALLY centered at y=450 with width 25px. Road must stay level in the nearest 60px on BOTH sides of every connection. Keep objects and sharp mountain peaks away from these strips.
3. TILE 3, the third quarter x1086..1628: the main road must ENTER from its left edge at y450, cross the rope suspension bridge in the middle, and EXIT its RIGHT edge at y450. Clearly show a continuous path to the right boundary. A scenic temple can remain higher in the distance, but the single main through-road cannot end at that temple or drop into a chasm. Keep a solid gray rock platform under the right edge with the same road and cliff height as tile 2. The rope bridge needs to be contained within this third tile and have both ends on platforms at the same approximate y450, not a diagonal vertical climb.
4. Tile 1 is an entrance cap: its road begins at the entrance gate and leaves only at its right edge. Tile 4 is an end cap: road arrives from its left edge and ends at palace stairs. Do not add an extra road leaving tile 4's far right edge.
5. Center the full red moon over tile 4 only and preserve neutral charcoal-gray skies at all connecting edges.

Result: no labels, no grid, no UI, no figures, no watermarks. A finished painted modular atlas with invisible boundaries, matching connecting ports and clear road through every piece. Preserve the rest of the painted artwork.
